title: The Promise Never Moves
author: Tshiamo Ramokgadi
body:
### The Promise Never Moves

There is a profound difference between knowing a truth in your head and watching it unfold in your life. As I sit down today, finally putting pen to paper, I can’t help but just sit back in absolute awe. My heart is full, completely overwhelmed by a single, undeniable reality: the faithfulness of my Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

*The promise never moves.*

What a heavy, beautiful way to kick off a first blog post. But before we get into the deep waters of what that actually means, let’s get the introductions out of the way. My name is Tshiamo Ramokgadi. I am Black, and yes, I have a blog. Everything I share on this platform, *ididntknowiwasme*, is driven by a simple, clear purpose: to edify the body of Christ, and to inspire anyone who happens to stumble across my words. If you are reading this right now, I want you to let this settle into your heart: God loves you, deeply and intentionally. And I do too.

To really understand the weight of the promise that never moves, we have to travel back in time to a day that changed the way I look at God.

The date was November 23, 2023.

Picture a freezing early morning at the base of the Kloofendal Nature Reserve. The Johannesburg sun hadn't quite broken through yet, and there I was, completely adamant about doing this hike. To paint a picture of Kloofendal, we all have one ultimate goal when we step onto those trails, and that is to reach the summit. At the very top, waiting for you on the peak, is a famous green chair. When you sit in it, it gives you a breathtaking view, literally overlooking the entire expanse of the Roodepoort area. That’s the goal. That’s the destination everyone is chasing, and on that freezing morning, I set foot on my own journey of achieving that summit.

But let's look at the unfiltered, unpolished version of the person standing at the starting line that day. I wasn't some perfect Christian influencer. If you looked at my life on paper, you would see a kid carrying a lot of broken pieces. I was broken-shoulder me. I was porn-watching me. I was failed-soccer-player me. I was college-dropout me.

I mention all of that baggage because I think a lot of us buy into the exhausting lie that we need to portray a flawless spiritual persona before God can ever speak to us. We think we have to clean up the mess and fix the addictions before we are allowed to encounter Him. But I am here to demystify that lie. That morning, I was just a normal 22-year-old kid who loved hiking, desperately trying to ignore the fact that my petrol gauge was sitting dead on empty.

Honestly, I shouldn't have even been there. My car was running on fumes. But something deep inside my spirit just got me out of bed, forced me into my shoes, and told me I had to get to that mountain. By the pure grace of God, I made it, found a parking spot, and stepped out into the crisp air.

When I finally stepped through the gates, the environment took my breath away. It was biting cold. The grass beneath my shoes was literally frozen, and my hands had become so numb they felt basically nonexistent. A thick, aggressive mist had rolled in, fighting the morning sunrise. You couldn't see anything. Heavy fog strips away the horizon. It takes away the big picture and forces you into a space where all you can see is the immediate, tiny step right in front of your feet. A lot of our lives look exactly like that fog. We beg God for the whole map, but He only illuminates the next few inches of the path.

I decided to take a completely new, unfamiliar pathway that morning. I stepped onto the dirt track and started walking. As I moved forward, the initial excitement carried me. I hit the first landmark, smiled to myself, and kept going. Five kilometers in, the reality of the trail started to set in. I began passing people some were already jogging down the mountain, finished and smiling, while others were still laboring upward alongside me. It felt like a living metaphor for the seasons of life.

By the ten-kilometer mark, the sun was starting to peek over the rugged edge of the mountain. You could feel the heat beginning to push against the cold, but the fog was stubborn. It stayed dense. I still couldn't see the peak. The trail was getting steeper, and my legs were starting to burn. I soldiered on, literally finding myself conversing with the birds in the trees and the wild plants along the path, just to distract my mind and catch my breath.

But by kilometer twenty, the romanticism completely evaporated. The exhaustion was real, and the self-doubt officially crept into my head. I stood there on the side of the path, chest heaving, wondering: *Am I even on the right path? Am I safe out here alone? Am I ever actually going to make it to the end?* If you have ever walked by faith, you know that exact internal panic. You feel exposed, you feel tired, and you feel entirely lost.

There were moments on that journey where it looked like absolutely nothing was happening, but I kept going. There were moments where I had to stop and rest, but still, I say the promise never moved. There were moments I sat completely down in the dirt, but yet, the promise never moved. I got lost. There were points where I couldn't see the finish line at all, but I kept moving. There were moments where the wind was my only guide and my faith was my only compass, and yet I kept going.

It was during this exact season of my life, wrestling with these heavy questions, that I penned a sermon in my notes. I was crying out just like Habakkuk 1:2: *“How long, Lord, must I call for help, but you do not listen?”* It felt like my own personal anthem. I felt unheard. I felt like the finish line was a myth. Yet, right underneath that cry, I wrote down a declaration that I had to hold onto: *The promise never moves, keep going!*

Then, suddenly, the mist parted for just a second, and I caught a glimpse of the finish line: the beloved green chair peak at the very top of the mountain. My heart absolutely soared. I smiled, thinking to myself, *“Yes! I’ll be up there in five minutes. It’s right there!”*

Spoiler alert: I was not there in five minutes.

Because of the unconventional, unfamiliar route I had chosen at the gate, the path didn't lead straight to the peak. Instead, it sharply veered away, forcing me to take the longest, most muscle-burning, winding way around the back of the mountain. I could *see* the finish line with my eyes, but I couldn't touch it with my hands. I had to keep pushing, putting one grueling foot in front of the other, even when the detour made absolutely no sense. Finally, after twenty-five long, exhausting kilometers... there she was. My beloved green chair. The finish line.

Many of our lives look exactly like that frustrating trail. God gives us a beautiful promise, yet the journey to that promise rarely looks like it is going to be fulfilled on our personal timeline. We face delays, we face fog, and we face detours that make us question if we heard God right in the first place.

But here is the breathtaking truth: The chair was there all along.

It never moved. It didn't get tired of waiting for me and pack up. It sat perfectly still, waiting for my arrival. And as I looked back down the mountain, I realized something beautiful. While I was walking the long way - winding through the brush, sweating, and questioning my own steps, wasn't wasting time. I was gaining the precise physical strength, the spiritual wisdom, and the emotional maturity I actually needed to sit in that chair properly.

The promise never moves is the journey of every single kid out there doing life. And the beautiful part about finally getting there, about reaching that peak, is that you gain perspective. From the top, looking out over the expanse of Roodepoort, you can see everyone who was right where you started. You can look down and see all the different paths you could have taken, realizing how each step shaped you.

But the absolute best thing? When you finally sit in that destination and look out into the horizon, you see another mountain just standing there, waiting to be conquered.

This platform, this blog, is the exact manifestation of a promise God whispered to my heart years ago. Habakkuk 2:2 tells us to *“Write the vision and make it plain on tablets, that he may run who reads it.”* That morning on the mountain, and in the months that followed, I wrote the vision down in my notes. I captured the sermon. But I had to wait. The vision was for an appointed time.

Now, three long years of walking through the dense fog, navigating my own failures, and taking the unconventional routes later, God has finally given me the platform to share it.

Do I have more to say now than I did back then? Yes. Am I more mature because of the delay? Unquestionably. Will these words impact more people because of the heavy miles it took to get here? Hella yes.

If you are in a season right now where you are walking entirely on faith, staring into a thick fog and wondering if you completely missed your turn, I want you to remember that the vision has been made plain: the promise never moves. Keep going! Do not sit down in the dirt permanently. One day, you will step out of the mist, you will finally reach your green chair, and the breathtaking view will make you realize exactly why He made you take the unconventional route.

**The promise hasn't moved an inch. It is simply waiting for you to finish the walk.**
